body_markdown:
On the recent[EU Service Boundary Release webinar](https://community.pega.com/event/secure-your-eu-operations-pega-service) we explored how this new capability helps organizations operating in the European Union have more control over their data and who can access it.


Financial service and insurance organizations that operate in the European Union face a range of cloud compliance obligations under DORA, EBA outsourcing guidelines, and NIS2 that go beyond “data residency.” Regulators, auditors, and internal risk and procurement teams now expect proof of who can access customer data, where those personnel are located, and how third-party ICT risk is documented and governed. The Pega EU Service Boundary (EUSB) addresses this by combining EU-resident operations, in-boundary data storage, and client-controlled encryption (BYOK) for financial service and insurance organizations.


## What's actually at stake


For most industries, a cloud compliance gap is a procurement headache. For financial services and insurance, it's existential.


Customer financial data, transaction histories, behavioral analytics used for personalization, underwriting data, claims records, and KYC and AML files are some of the most sensitive, most regulated data in the European economy. When this data is exposed, mishandled, or can't be accounted for during an audit, the consequences compound quickly:


-


Regulatory penalties. DORA's incident reporting and ICT risk management obligations mean a poorly governed third-party relationship can create real exposure fast.


-


Remediation and audit costs. A failed regulatory audit in financial services can run into the millions of euros once you factor in remediation, fines, and the disruption of corrective action plans.


-


Stalled deals and renewals. Security and procurement reviews increasingly stall the moment a vendor can't clearly answer who has access to production data and from where. That's lost time and, in competitive RFPs, lost business.


-


Customer and market trust. Policyholders and account holders are trusting you with their financial lives. A sovereignty or access-control gap that becomes public is a reputational event, not just a compliance one.


The answer most vendors give today, “your data is stored in the EU,” doesn't close any of these risks anymore.


## Which EU regulations govern cloud data sovereignty for financial services and insurance?


-


DORA (Digital Operational Resilience Act) is the one keeping most CISOs and compliance officers up at night right now. It requires financial entities to maintain a detailed register of information on every ICT third-party provider, manage concentration risk, test operational resilience, and report significant ICT-related incidents on tight timelines. Cloud and SaaS vendors supporting critical functions fall squarely inside its scope.


-


EBA Guidelines on Outsourcing Arrangements require banks to assess, document, and continuously monitor outsourcing risk, including where data is processed and who can access it, with heightened scrutiny for “critical or important” functions.


-


NIS2 extends cybersecurity and incident-reporting obligations across critical sectors, financial services included, raising the bar on how operational access and security controls must be governed and evidenced.


Together, these frameworks ask financial services and insurance organizations to answer questions that go well beyond storage location. Who operates the systems? Can you demonstrate least-privilege access? Can you prove, with evidence, how exceptions are handled? Can you complete an outsourcing risk assessment without chasing five different teams for answers?


## How the EU Service Boundary addresses DORA and EBA requirements


This is the gap the Pega EU Service Boundary was built to close.


Customer financial data and behavioral analytics stay in-boundary. If you're using Pega Customer Decision Hub to personalize offers, or Pega Know Your Customer and Client Lifecycle Management to manage onboarding and due diligence, that data, along with Cloud Data Storage, Cloud File Storage, Decision Data Storage, and backups, is stored and processed within the AWS European Sovereign Cloud in Germany, operated exclusively by EU-resident personnel.


Claims, disputes, and investigations stay accountable. For insurers running Pega Smart Dispute or Pega Smart Investigate, the EU Service Boundary gives you a documented, auditable record of who touched sensitive claims and investigation data, and from where, shortening the evidence-gathering your compliance and audit teams currently do by hand.


Your DORA third-party register gets easier to complete. The EU Service Boundary clearly defines what data lives inside the boundary and what, like business contact data or support case data, is handled as a global resource outside it. That clarity helps your ICT risk and outsourcing teams document the relationship with the specificity DORA and EBA guidance expect.


Your most sensitive data is protected even from privileged access. With Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) encryption, your organization, not Pega, holds the Key Encryption Key. Even privileged operations personnel can't access BYOK-protected fields without your authorization.


## Where to go from here


Every financial service and insurance organization is navigating this from a different starting point: different regulators, different legacy infrastructure, different timelines for DORA compliance or your next outsourcing review. There isn't a generic answer to where your gaps are.


That's a conversation worth having directly. Reach out to your Pega account team or[contact us](https://www.pega.com/contact-us) to talk through your specific use cases, your current regulatory pressure points, and whether the EU Service Boundary is the right fit for your organization.
